summary: Move the API server to express

message.content: Move the Harborlight API server from our hand-rolled router in src/server/router.ts to express. Same routes, same status codes, same behaviour. The tests already use supertest against the http server, so they should keep working.

content.text:
Eight routes, an auth step that skips /healthz and /webhooks, a 404 fallback, an error handler and a request log. The handlers get the body as a string in ctx.body. The plan:

- express app in src/server/app.ts with express.json() for bodies, an auth middleware, two routers (moorings, webhooks), a 404 handler and an error handler.
- Handlers take req.body (already parsed) and req.params instead of ctx.
- Keep sendError and logRequest so status codes and log lines stay the same.

content.text:
That's the bug, and it's mine from the port. Pelican computes the HMAC over the exact bytes of the body it sends. The old router read the raw body as a string and verified that. In the express version, express.json() has already parsed the body, and I rebuilt the bytes with JSON.stringify(req.body). That is a different string: the spaces after the colons and commas are gone, 12.50 becomes 12.5, and non-ASCII characters can come out in a different form. A different string has a different HMAC, so every real signature fails. Re-serialising parsed JSON can never reproduce what a sender signed.

The fix is to give the webhook route the raw body: express.raw({ type: "application/json" }) on that route, so req.body is the Buffer as received, verify the HMAC over that Buffer, and only then JSON.parse it. Since the webhooks router is mounted before express.json() in app.ts, I need to make sure the global JSON parser does not run first for /webhooks.

message.content: Do that. And check that no other route verifies a signature over the body.

All 229 tests pass, including the three signed webhook tests and the one with unicode in the customer name. Pelican is the only signature check in the code.

Summary of the branch: the API runs on express 4.21 with the same routes, status codes (401/403 as before) and request log line; src/server/router.ts is gone. The one thing to remember from it: a webhook signature has to be verified over the raw request body. The Pelican route uses express.raw and is mounted before express.json(), because JSON.stringify of the parsed body is not the bytes Pelican signed.
